summary.intent: Land slice 2 of ADR 0026 (checker converter, PR #394) and related PRs, accept the ADR, design a semantic fix for the field-cap regression, resolve review findings and merge conflicts on change #191, and wrap up the session.
summary.outcome: Most work merged to main (parity check, ADR 0026 acceptance, changesets, 0.10.0 release PR), and the cap/Omit design for slice 3 was verified against real tsrs. PR #394 is not finished: 6 findings remain open, fixes are only uncommitted in a worker's worktree, and a merge conflict with main persists. The 0.10.0 release was still publishing.

repo: Checker converter caps live in convert.rs: MAX_FIELDS=[100,40], MAX_MEMBERS=[500,120], MAX_DEPTH=5.
Structural collapse policy (ADR 0012) collapses DOM/ARIA/style families to names past 30 props and other dependency sources past 200.
PropType::HtmlAttributes { element, omitted } exists, so it can carry an element and an omit list; element mapping lives in resolver/html.rs.
The converter's react_terminal handles only ReactNode, ReactElement, JSX.Element, ElementType and CSSProperties; it has no ComponentProps*/HTMLAttributes family recognition.
Nothing in crates/semantic or tsc-client calls getBaseTypes yet; the Rust client also cannot read questionToken/initializer through declaration nodes, unlike the Node SDK prototype.
OpaqueDetail::new is pub(crate) in a different crate from convert.rs, so degraded_type is the required public seam.

Checker evaluates away written alias names like ComponentPropsWithoutRef; recognition must walk the Omit/Partial alias-argument chain to the React interface and read the element from its type argument. getAliasTypeArguments is a method on the type object, not the checker.
Own vs inherited members can be split deterministically by declaration path (BoxProps: 2 own in fixture, 263 in @types/react).
react/34's structural-path output is just a bare Named{BoxProps}, so it is green only because the checker golden is also the bare name.
Main's release workflow runs on every push to main and spawns chained runs; the first skipped 0.9.0 as already published then dispatched the next.
PR conflict on #394 is in apps/oracle/package.json between construct:checker and #392's construct:parity script plus pinned tsrs devDependency.
The release consumed existing changesets, so .changeset/checker-states-every-type.md must be re-verified after merging main.

code.finding: PropType::HtmlAttributes { element, omitted } variant definition; can express family plus omitted keys.

workflow: When a worker is pushing to a branch, route merges through that same worker to avoid push races between two writers.
Verify design claims against real binaries/APIs before committing to them; this caught a wrong claim about react/34 and the lost alias name.
Group review findings by pattern, write a failing test first for each, and dismiss non-reproducing findings with evidence.
A workflow in action_required or cancelled state is not a failure; check conclusions before reporting a release as failed.
Subagent reports carry no user authority; the classifier denies remote branch deletion so those need user-run commands.

friction: User repeatedly asked whether #394 findings were fixed; the worker ran 33+ minutes without pushing, leaving only uncommitted local edits (about 49k added lines mostly regenerated recordings).
Misread interned structural output required several probe iterations to inspect.
My initial claim that the structural path handles react/34 with own members plus layers was wrong and had to be corrected.
Probe script errors around the alias-argument API required multiple reruns.
Release appeared failed to the user but was just slow (Windows build); extra release runs on non-release main pushes and a stray #396 version PR caused confusion.
Heavy machine load (load average 52) made speed measurements noisy.
Remote branch deletion denied by classifier; about 40 stale worktrees remain.
